newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Big Swiss banks set to report booming H1 profit.
newsitem.headline: Big Swiss banks set to report booming H1 profit.

text.p: Switzerland's "Big Three" global banks are expected to report that profits soared in the first half of 1997 on the back of booming world equity markets, leaner organisation and huge write-offs for bad loans last year.
Analysts forecast leaps of between 40 or 50 percent in net profit at Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS ), which will be the first to report next Tuesday.
Estimates are mostly higher still for Swiss Bank Corp (SBC), due on August 13, and Credit Suisse Group, which plans to announce its six-month figures on August 27.
"Strong growth in commission income and trading income is what drove the profit increases at all three banks," Susanne Borer at Bank Vontobel in Zurich told Reuters.
Surging income from trading and commissions is a common element among many banks this year as world equity markets flourish.
The gains in equities have created a rising tide of assets worldwide which must be reinvested, and these are benefitting fund managers at Swiss banks.

In addition, the three banks took huge extraordinary write-offs last year totalling about 10 billion Swiss francs ($6.6 billion) to settle a backlog of bad loans that had been swallowing an increasingly large part of net profit.
The three banks' profits all suffered last year from high loan-loss provisions and credit losses in their domestic business as a result of a sharp and lasting downturn in the Swiss economy.
"The restructuring plans aimed at focusing business more clearly and cutting costs seem to be making progress," added Christoph Meiri at Zurich Kantonalbank (ZKB).

Meiri, whose forecasts are on the high side of the market, expects UBS net profit after minorities to rise 51 percent to 1.67 billion Swiss francs and total 3.03 billion Swiss francs for the full year 1997.
UBS last year posted first-half net of 1.11 billion but a full-year loss of 348 million after taking extraordinary provisions of three billion and 120 million for restructuring.
For SBC, Meiri forecasts a jump of 69 percent to 1.22 billion Swiss francs and for full 1997 net profit after minorities of 2.28 billion Swiss francs.

SBC saw first-half 1996 net profit of 722 million Swiss francs. It posted a loss for 1996 of 1.95 billion on extraordinary charges for bad credits and a change in provisioning methods to cut down future losses.
Credit Suisse Group's net after minorities should be an impressive 90 percent higher in the first six months at 1.58 billion Swiss francs, Meiri said.
"Credit Suisse Group was the most heavily burdened by bad Swiss loans and therefore should benefit the most from last year's extraordinary provisioning," he said.
Full-year net profit should total 2.18 billion Swiss francs.
CS Group net in the 1996 first half was 830 million Swiss francs and for 1996 as a whole 2.43 billion.
Bank Vontobel's Borer was more subdued in her forecasts than ZKB's Meiri.
She expects UBS first-half net to rise 47 percent to 1.62 billion, SBC to jump 55 percent to 1.12 billion and CS Group to rise 42 percent to 1.18 billion Swiss francs.

Bank Sarasin analyst Franco Catanzaro has forecast a half-year net profit jump at UBS of 48 percent to 1.64 billion Swiss francs, 63 percent at SBC to 1.18 billion and 48 percent at CS Group to 1.23 billion. -- Zurich Newsroom, +41-1-631 7340 ($ = 1.513 Swiss Francs)
